title: Approve tiered SLO targets (Hosted vs Dedicated) for Q1 reliability program
creator: Evelyn Hart
description:
Objective
- Negotiate and formally approve tiered SLO targets (Hosted vs Dedicated) that are measurable with our canonical SLIs and realistic given infra headroom + routing/fallback behavior.
- Record rationale and customer expectations, including how these targets map to customer-facing SLA language and support escalation posture.

Context
- This is the Product approval checkpoint for the Q1 reliability milestone: tiered SLOs (availability, latency, streaming reliability) + enforced error budget policy.
- Drivers: recurring escalations re latency spikes + 5xx/stream disconnects under burst traffic; need alignment between Product SLAs and engineering measurement/enforcement.

Scope
- In-scope request paths: chat/completions, embeddings, streaming.
- In-scope tiers: Hosted (shared) and Dedicated (reserved capacity).
- Reporting: per-region and global rollups using a 28-day rolling window (with weekly views for faster iteration).
- Exclusions (consistent across tiers): invalid requests (4xx), rate-limited (429), explicit customer-configured blocks, client-aborted streams (client disconnect before first token / explicit cancel). Retries/fallback are accounted per SLI spec (see links).

Proposed targets (FINAL)
Notes:
- Latency is end-to-end at the API boundary (gateway receive -> final response for non-stream; gateway receive -> first token for stream). We will also track TTFT and full-stream duration as supporting metrics, but SLO is on TTFT.
- Success-rate SLO uses "request success" semantics (non-5xx, plus streaming disconnect/error events classified as server-side failures).

1) Hosted (shared)
- Availability (success rate): 99.50% per region (28d)
- Chat/Completions (non-stream) latency: p95 <= 2.5s (28d)
- Chat/Completions (streaming) latency: p95 TTFT <= 1.2s (28d)
- Embeddings latency: p95 <= 600ms (28d)
- Streaming reliability: server-side stream disconnect/error rate <= 0.30% (28d)

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Availability (success rate): 99.90% per region (28d)
- Chat/Completions (non-stream) latency: p95 <= 1.8s (28d)
- Chat/Completions (streaming) latency: p95 TTFT <= 900ms (28d)
- Embeddings latency: p95 <= 450ms (28d)
- Streaming reliability: server-side stream disconnect/error rate <= 0.10% (28d)

Guardrails / clarifications for customer expectation-setting
- SLOs are measured at Redwood’s API boundary. Customer network conditions are not included; however, server-side stream disconnects do count.
- During overload mitigation, we may:
  (a) shed load for Hosted (429/overload) to protect fleet health; 429 is excluded from availability SLI but will be visible in dashboards as "overload shed".
  (b) route/fallback within Dedicated pools first; cross-tier fallback is not expected behavior and should be treated as an incident-worthy misconfiguration.
- We will publish per-tier status impact; Dedicated communications will call out region + scope (account-specific where possible) rather than broad "API degraded" statements.

Rationale / trade-offs (why these numbers)
- Dedicated targets are tighter due to:
  - reserved capacity + explicit headroom commitments (Infra agreed to minimum headroom targets per region and faster escalation path to fleet ops)
  - reduced tail-latency from noisy-neighbor effects relative to Hosted
  - customer expectation: Dedicated is sold with "predictability" (lower variance matters more than median wins)
- Hosted targets balance:
  - multi-tenant burst behavior and protection mechanisms (overload shedding, rate-limit spikes)
  - ability to keep the platform stable during global traffic events without over-provisioning
  - need to avoid setting SLOs that force perpetual error-budget exhaustion and block improvements during the first enforcement phase
- Streaming reliability targets explicitly respond to customer-reported disconnects; we need a visible, auditable SLI here (not buried as generic 5xx).

Approvals
- Product: Evelyn Hart (CPO) approved targets and expectation language on 2026-02-11.
- Hosted PM owner: Nikhil Sharma approved Hosted targets on 2026-02-11.
- Dedicated PM owner: Lauren Bishop approved Dedicated targets on 2026-02-11.
- SRE: Rafael Mendes + Aisha Bello confirmed measurability + burn-rate alerting compatibility.
- Infra: Neha Kapoor confirmed capacity headroom posture is compatible with Dedicated p95 targets (with explicit mitigation runbooks).

Deliverables / next steps
- Update Confluence canonical doc with the final targets + rationale and link to this ticket.
- PM-815: finalize SLA mapping language and confirm exclusions match contractual expectations.
- Ensure dashboards expose: per-tier, per-region, top contributors (model/route), and explicit streaming failure breakdown.
- Coordinate CS enablement: escalation posture by tier and what data to request (request IDs, regions, model, timestamps).

- SLI spec (measurement + exclusions): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/sli-specification-api-gateway-and-routing.json
- Error budget policy: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/error-budget-policy-and-enforcement.json
- Hosted/Dedicated SLO definitions (canonical): sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/tiered-slo-definitions-hosted-vs-dedicated.json
acceptance_criteria: Targets approved by Hosted PM + Dedicated PM + CPO, with SRE + Infra sign-off recorded
Targets expressed in terms of canonical SLIs (success rate, p95 latency, streaming disconnect/error rate) with clear exclusions
Per-tier customer expectation notes documented (fallback, overload shedding, boundary of measurement)
Targets handed off to Eng for implementation in SLO config + dashboards + alerting
comments: 2026-01-24 (Nikhil Sharma): Pulled latest proposal from the working sheet. Biggest contention is Hosted p95 latency; recommend keeping it at 2.5s to avoid permanent red while we stabilize tier tagging + streaming SLI classification. Dedicated can be tighter given reserved headroom and routing constraints.

2026-01-28 (Lauren Bishop): Dedicated customers explicitly ask for TTFT and stream reliability, not just non-5xx. Please ensure streaming disconnect/error is a first-class SLI. For Dedicated, p95 TTFT 900ms feels achievable if EU-W headroom is enforced (see recent SUP-28455 pattern).

2026-02-03 (Aisha Bello): Confirmed we can compute all proposed SLIs with the ingress tier tags + stream event taxonomy. Reminder: 429/overload shed excluded from availability SLI, but we should dashboard it separately so PM/CS can explain 'why' when customers see throttling.

2026-02-05 (Neha Kapoor): Infra can commit to Dedicated headroom targets, but we need explicit 'capacity escalation' triggers tied to burn-rate alerts (not just reactive paging). Please align targets with the capacity mitigation guidelines runbook so on-call actions are concrete.

2026-02-10 (Evelyn Hart): Approving approach contingent on clear customer-facing expectation language: (1) measurement boundary at API, (2) tier-specific comms, (3) no cross-tier fallback for Dedicated without incident declaration. Proceed and sync with PM-815 for SLA wording.

2026-02-11 (Nikhil Sharma): Final targets accepted as written. Request that Console shows both per-tier and Hosted-vs-Dedicated comparison to help Sales/CS explain value of Dedicated. Marking done; implementation follows ENG-4926 + dashboard workstream.
